title: Test and wording gaps from the WCLI-138 delta review (LOWs, none blocking)
description: Follow-ups from the Opus delta review APPROVE at dc37c02 of ward-cli#262 (WCLI-138). Tests: (1) readStdinValueBytes(8, fd) over exactly 8 bytes, since changing > to >= at the bound still passes; (2) the backspace-zeroing claim is vacuous because the final fill(0) satisfies it, so add a real control through scripted ports (readHiddenValueBytes would need ports) or reword the comments in secret.test.ts and passphrase.test.ts; (3) the single-buffer test should assert through a read port that every target.buffer === scratch.buffer.buffer; (4) neither arm of defaultWait and the real readSync offset path are exercised (a pipe fed in two writes would cover it), and the readHidden writePrompt guard has no test. Wording: readHidden in secrets.ts says undefined on cancel but Ctrl-C returns an empty buffer; the passphrase header says Ctrl-C keeps what was typed but the reader throws; the secret-value.ts comment above readHiddenValueBytes credits backspace zeroing where the fixed array is what guarantees it; doc comments sit above StdinReadScratch and PassphraseReadScratch instead of their functions; secrets.ts line 60 is about 130 columns.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each test gap above has a test that goes red when the behaviour is removed, or its comment is reworded to what is true
The contract and doc-comment wording items above are corrected

implementationNotes: Implemented on fix/WCLI-142-delta-review-lows. Tests: exact-bound stdin (a >= mutation goes red there only); single-buffer identity asserted through a read port; real readSync offset path over a FIFO fed in two writes; defaultWait split into an exported waitReadable with poll and sleep ports so both arms are asserted (swapping the arm goes red); the post-read writePrompt guard in readHidden. Backspace-zeroing: reworded source and test comments rather than adding a control, since the final fill(0) is what guarantees it. Wording: readHidden contract (Ctrl-C returns empty, undefined only for an unreadable terminal), passphrase header (Ctrl-C throws), doc comments moved onto their functions, long line wrapped. bun run check green: 1225 pass. Mutations run: bound check, second-buffer allocation, wait-arm inversion.

Folded in as new commits on the same branch: the readHidden contract in secrets.ts now says a raw-mode failure throws and names the !available() path; the waitReadable test fixture is result 0 / revents 0 so a result>0 mutation goes red (run, red); the FIFO test now orders its two writes by a handshake and records reads through a port (asserts at least two non-zero reads), opens the FIFO non-blocking with a 5s deadline so a writer that never starts fails rather than hangs (run, fails at 5s); defaultWait's production plumbing is stated plainly as not covered.

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES
Review of opum-ai/ward-cli#271 (WCLI-142) at head 5a48886337018a10fc32f6ac6120bbd67e28cc41. This is a tree read only: I ran no tests and no mutations.

FINDINGS

1. BLOCKING, src/application/secrets.ts:52-55. The reworded readHidden contract says "undefined when the terminal cannot be read or put into raw mode". The raw-mode half is false at this head. In src/adapters/secret-value.ts, readHidden calls writePrompt (:293) and then setRaw(true) (:294), and both run before the try at :299. readHidden has no outer catch, so defaultSetRaw's Error("no raw mode") propagates out of readHidden instead of returning undefined. No test drives setRaw(true) throwing through createTerminalSecretValues. The passphrase adapter is different: its read() catches every non-WardError and returns undefined (passphrase.ts:204-210), so the same claim is true there. This task's AC index 1 is "contract wording corrected", and this rewording adds a new untrue clause to a secret-handling contract. The fix is wording only and in scope: drop "or put into raw mode", or say the raw-mode failure throws. Moving setRaw(true) inside the try would change behaviour, which the task does not allow. A smaller point in the same contract: it doesn't mention the !available() → undefined path (secret-value.ts:292).

2. LOW, test/secret.test.ts, the test "the wait polls for readability first and sleeps only where poll did not resolve". The comment says "A poll that answered, even with nothing readable, ends the wait", but the stub returns { result: 1, revents: 1 }, and POLLIN is 0x1 (terminal-input.ts:47). So the fixture is the readable case. A mutation to `poll(...)?.result > 0` would stay green even though the comment says that case is covered. Fix: use { result: 0, revents: 0 } or reword the comment.

3. LOW, secret-value.ts:111-113, defaultWait and its default sleep. Both arms of waitReadable's decision are now asserted through ports, and swapping the arms goes red. The production plumbing is still unexercised, because the EAGAIN test injects its own wait. Each of these mutations stays green: turning defaultWait into a no-op, dropping its waitReadable call, or breaking the default Atomics.wait sleep lambda (:104-106). Item (4) is therefore only partly closed; I don't consider it blocking.

4. LOW, test/secret.test.ts, the test "a stdin read over a real descriptor fed in two writes keeps both, at the right offsets". Whether it covers the offset path depends on timing. Nothing asserts that more than one readSync happened. If the reader stalls more than 300 ms before its first read (a loaded ARM64 runner), it gets "firstsecond" in one read, and a `subarray(length)` → `buffer` mutation stays green. The failure mode is a false green, not a flake. Also, if the sh writer never opens the FIFO, openSync(fifo, "r") blocks the test process synchronously and the bun test timeout can't interrupt it. Possible fix: also read the FIFO through a recording read port that wraps readSync, and assert at least two non-zero reads.

ITEMS VERIFIED TRUE OR RED AT THIS HEAD
- (1) Exact-8 bound. withInput writes a regular file, so all 8 bytes arrive in one readSync into the 9-byte buffer. With `>=` at secret-value.ts:252, 8 >= 8 throws, and the expectation of "a"*8 goes red. The 9-byte case above refuses under either operator, so the claim "goes red here and nowhere above" holds.
- (3) Single-buffer identity. The read port records buffer.buffer on every call, including the final 0-byte read, and the count is source.length+1. A second allocation, or reading into a temporary and copying, changes the backing ArrayBuffer and goes red. `new Uint8Array(n)` is never pooled, so the identity check is sound.
- (4c) writePrompt("\n") guard. Remove the catch at :330-334 and the throw escapes the finally, so readHidden throws "terminal gone" and the test goes red. [true,false] raw ordering holds.
- (2) Backspace zeroing was reworded, not given a control, which the AC allows. The new source comments (secret-value.ts:178-182, passphrase.ts:74-77) are true: held[--count] = 0 at :208 and :103, and the final fill(0) is the guarantee. The new test comments in both files are true. The passphrase run() does assert peak (passphrase.test.ts:216), so "pins the result and the peak" holds.
- Passphrase header (passphrase.ts:19-21): Ctrl-D breaks and submits, Ctrl-C throws backup_passphrase_rejected whatever was typed (:100). True.
- The readHidden contract's Ctrl-C clause is true: 0x03 returns new Uint8Array(0) at :205, and the caller rejects empty and undefined alike (secrets.ts:380, :384).
- Doc comments now sit on readStdinValueBytes and readPassphraseBytes, with their own short comments on StdinReadScratch and PassphraseReadScratch. The long secrets.ts line is wrapped.
- Production behaviour: the only src change beyond comments is defaultWait → waitReadable, which is behaviour-preserving (same pollInput(descriptor, QUIET_MS=30) and then the Atomics.wait sleep). The new WaitPorts seam touches no secret bytes: it carries only a descriptor and timeouts. Zeroing and single-buffer invariants are unchanged in all three readers.
- DEC-182 (1) fences: none touched. No CI, deps or lockfile, settings, hooks or build change. The new test spawns only mkfifo and sh, writes only under the test's mkdtemp root (removed afterAll), and uses synthetic bytes.
- The .quest/tasks/WCLI-142.json diff only moves status to In Progress and adds an implementation note. Both ACs are still unchecked, which fits an open PR.

COULD NOT VERIFY FROM A TREE READ
- That the suite is green (implementation note: 1225 pass; CI reports Check, Docs and Tracker integrity green). I did not run it.
- That the mutations the implementer reports (bound, second buffer, wait-arm inversion) actually went red. I reasoned about them but did not execute them.
- FIFO timing on the mbpm2 linux-arm64 runner, so whether CI's run of the FIFO test actually took two reads.
- Runtime behaviour of defaultSetRaw on a real non-raw-capable stdin. Finding 1 rests on code order, not on an observed run.

VERDICT: APPROVE
Round-2 full review of opum-ai/ward-cli#271 (WCLI-142) at e02a1f7d9fac55c9e179ec367c6371b89b5221f1. I read the tree only; I ran no tests or mutations. Model: claude-opus-5-5, a model reviewer unit, not a human.

ROUND-1 CLAIMS, CHECKED
1. BLOCKING (readHidden contract): fixed. The contract at src/application/secrets.ts:55-60 now matches the code order in src/adapters/secret-value.ts:
   - `!available()` returns undefined at :296.
   - writePrompt (:297) and setRaw(true) (:298) both run before the try at :303, so a raw-mode failure throws before the read starts.
   - A non-WardError from the read becomes undefined at :346. A WardError is rethrown at :345.
   - Ctrl-C returns `new Uint8Array(0)` at :209. The caller rejects empty and undefined the same way, at secrets.ts:382 and :386.
   - The undefined cases the contract lists are all of them (:296 and :346). setRaw was not moved.
2. LOW (wait fixture): fixed. test/secret.test.ts now uses { result: 0, revents: 0 }. A `poll(...)?.result > 0` mutation calls sleep, so calls becomes ["poll 9 30","sleep 30"] and the test goes red. The comment is true of waitReadable at secret-value.ts:107.
3. LOW (defaultWait): reworded, but the new wording is partly untrue. See finding L1.
4. LOW (FIFO): fixed, and deterministic: it cannot pass falsely. The writer sends "second" only after the first-read-done marker exists. The read port creates that marker only after a read returned more than 0 bytes, and those bytes can only come from "first". So at least two non-zero reads always happen, and one read can never take both writes. If the writer's 200-iteration fallback ever fired first, the `sizes >= 2` assertion would go red rather than pass.

FINDINGS (none blocking)
L1. LOW, src/adapters/secret-value.ts:111. "Not covered by a test" is no longer accurate. The FIFO test overrides only the `read` port, so readOnce (:129) falls back to the real defaultWait on every EAGAIN. The handshake makes an EAGAIN between the two writes almost certain, so defaultWait, waitReadable and the real pollInput do run; nothing asserts what they do. The rest of the comment holds: "a no-op here would still pass" and "would only spin" are true. The Atomics.wait sleep lambda really is not run wherever libc's poll resolves. Suggested wording: "run by the FIFO test when a read reports EAGAIN, but not asserted". This touches AC-1's "reworded to what is true", but the substance stands, so I rate it LOW.
L2. LOW, the FIFO test in test/secret.test.ts (the `for (let waited = 0; !existsSync(opened) && waited < 500; ...)` loop). That deadline is 500 × Bun.sleep(10), so at least 5000 ms. The test passes no timeout argument and bunfig.toml sets none, so bun's default 5000 ms per-test timeout applies. For a writer that never opens the FIFO, bun's timeout most likely fires first. The reported "fails at 5.0 s" is then the harness failing the test, not the `expect(existsSync(opened))` assertion. The abandoned async body's finally may then run during a later test. It still fails rather than hangs, which is the point. A cleaner fix is a shorter loop (for example 300 × 10 ms) or an explicit test timeout above the deadline.
L3. LOW, the same test's finally. It never kills the writer. Suppose the writer spawns late and opens the FIFO only after `closeSync(descriptor)` has run. Its blocking `exec 3>"$1"` then has no reader, so it blocks forever, `await writer.exited` never resolves, and the sh child leaks. That needs a spawn slower than about 5 s, so it is rare, and only on a path that is already failing. Fix: call `writer.kill()` before `await writer.exited`. Killing after a normal exit is harmless. Separately, if Bun.spawn itself threw, `descriptor` would leak, because the spawn sits outside the try. That is trivial.
Note (not a finding): the contract still leaves out two throws that predate this PR. A failure of the initial writePrompt throws (:297), and secret_value_multiline is thrown. Neither is claimed false and neither is in this task's scope.

A. TRUTH OF CONTRACTS AND COMMENTS: all true except L1.
- secrets.ts readHidden (:55-60) and readStdin (:62-65): true.
- Passphrase header (passphrase.ts:19-21): Ctrl-D breaks (:101). Ctrl-C throws backup_passphrase_rejected (:100), and read() rethrows that WardError (:206). True.
- The backspace comments at secret-value.ts:183-186 and passphrase.ts:74-77: true. Removing a byte zeroes its slot (:212 and :103), and the final fill(0) at :221 and :113 is what guarantees the zeroing.
- Doc comments now sit on readStdinValueBytes and readPassphraseBytes. The long line is wrapped.
- Test comments: true. That covers the passphrase.test.ts and secret.test.ts backspace notes, the "every read, the final empty one included" note, the "A read before the writer holds its end reports end of input" note, and the wait-fixture note.

B. AC-1 MUTATIONS, ONE PER ITEM
(1) Exact bound: changing `>` to `>=` at secret-value.ts:256 throws on 8 >= 8, so the exact-8 case goes red. The 9-byte case refuses under either operator.
(2) Backspace zeroing: reworded rather than given a control, which the AC allows. No mutation applies, and the comments are true.
(3) Single buffer: allocating a second array, or reading into a temporary and copying, changes the backing store `buffer.buffer`. The `targets.every(t => t === scratch.buffer?.buffer)` check goes red. The count of reads (`source.length + 1`) is pinned too.
(4a) Wait arms: swapping the arms, or the `result > 0` mutation, goes red.
(4b) Offset path: changing `buffer.subarray(length)` to `buffer` at :253 yields "second" followed by five zero bytes, so `toBe("firstsecond")` goes red.
(4c) writePrompt guard: remove the catch at :334-338 and "terminal gone" escapes the finally, so the test goes red. The raw sequence [true,false] is asserted.
(4d) defaultWait: a no-op stays green, which the comment states (L1 is about the "not covered" wording only).

C. FIFO: deterministic, and bounded with the caveats in L2 and L3.
- Opening the read end O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK succeeds immediately with no writer, on both Linux and darwin. sh then opens the write end blocking, and that succeeds at once because a reader exists. No synchronous openSync can block.
- A read before any writer would return 0 (EOF). The opened marker guards against that.
- A read with a writer but no data throws EAGAIN; on Linux EAGAIN and EWOULDBLOCK are the same value. readOnce handles both codes.
- After the marker appears, the read loop is fully synchronous (readSync plus the FFI poll), so bun's timeout cannot interrupt it. It is bounded by the child's logic, about 200 × 0.05 s, not by the test. On the happy path it lasts roughly one writer poll interval.
- If the reader closes while sh is mid-printf, SIGPIPE ends sh. The finally's marker write releases the writer's wait loop.
- The child writes nothing to its stdout pipe, so it cannot deadlock on a full pipe.
- Everything is created under a mkdtemp directory inside `root`, which afterAll removes recursively.
- `sleep 0.05`, `$((i+1))` and `[ -e ]` work in dash with coreutils or busybox. If fractional sleep were unsupported, the test would go red, not pass falsely.

D. PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: unchanged.
- In the six-file PR diff, the only change to src code is extracting defaultWait into the exported waitReadable. It makes the same pollInput(descriptor, QUIET_MS) call with the same `!== undefined` early return, and the same Atomics.wait(QUIET_MS) sleep.
- The StdinReadScratch move is type-only. Everything else is comments.
- The WaitPorts seam carries only a descriptor and timeouts, never secret bytes. Zeroing and the single buffer are unchanged in all three readers.
- The new test ports record only ArrayBuffer identity and read sizes, never content, and all fixture bytes are synthetic.
- The r1-to-r2 diff also shows src/application/unregister.ts, src/contract/errors.ts and test/unregister.test.ts. Those arrived with the a60b7ed merge of origin/dev (WCLI-143, opum-ai/ward-cli#272), are absent from the merge-base diff, and are not WCLI-142 changes.

E. DEC-182 (1) FENCES: none touched. The PR's file set is .quest/tasks/WCLI-142.json and five src/test files. There is no CI, dependency or lockfile, settings, hooks, build or auth change. The new test spawns only mkfifo and sh. The tracker diff sets the status to In Progress and adds two implementation notes. Both ACs are still unchecked, which fits an open PR.

COULD NOT VERIFY FROM A TREE READ
- That the suite and CI are green at e02a1f7, and that the reported mutations (bound, second buffer, wait arm, result>0) and the 5 s failure of a never-opening writer actually happened as the tracker note says.
- Whether CI's linux-arm64 run of the FIFO test actually hit EAGAIN, and so ran defaultWait. The handshake makes that near-certain but I did not observe it.
- That Bun's fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK and readSync behave as POSIX does on a nonblocking FIFO, throwing EAGAIN rather than retrying internally. Either behaviour gives the same result.
- Whether `bun test` exits or hangs when the L3 case leaves a ref'd Bun.spawn child blocked in open(2).
- That the .quest record was written through quest rather than edited by hand.
finalSummary: The WCLI-138 delta-review test and wording gaps closed in ward-cli#271 (squash 46df9b5) after two Opus-model review rounds, both recorded verbatim in the notes. Three non-blocking LOWs from round 2 are filed as WCLI-147.
